claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure has well-defined phase boundaries.
The hierarchical heterostructure exhibits grain-size variability.
The proposed machine-learning model integrates phase distribution, grain size, and interface characteristics extracted from microstructural imaging.
Phase boundaries mediate local stress concentration and crack initiation.
Grain-size distribution mediates local stress concentration and crack initiation.
Interface properties mediate local stress concentration and crack initiation.
The model can learn correlations between hierarchical microstructural descriptors and mechanical responses.
Microstructure-informed machine learning can capture local stress variations and crack-propagation triggers that continuum models average out.
The framework can predict Young's modulus for HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile testing.
The framework can predict yield strength for HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile testing.
The framework can predict fracture initiation behavior for HfNbTiVAl10.
The framework will reduce prediction error margins by at least 10% relative to established finite-element or continuum simulations.
The framework will reduce computational prediction time by approximately 50% relative to established simulations.
Conventional finite-element and continuum methods are slower for this prediction task.
Conventional finite-element and continuum methods have larger predictive error margins under comparable test conditions.
Insufficient microstructural imaging resolution may prevent the hypothesized gains.
Unaccounted environmental or dynamic damage mechanisms may prevent the hypothesized gains.
Extreme heterogeneity may prevent robust feature extraction and cause the hypothesis to fail.
